title: When Everyone Else Seems to Be Living Better
subtitle: 社群媒體與錯失恐懼
source: 原創教學文章；心理學概念為一般知識，非特定研究報導

beginner.title: The Photos That Changed Mia’s Mood
paras: Mia had a good Saturday. She read a novel, cooked lunch with her father, and helped her younger brother with his homework. In the evening, she felt calm and satisfied. Then she opened a social media app.
Mia 度過了愉快的星期六。她讀了小說、和爸爸一起煮午餐，也幫弟弟寫功課。晚上她感到平靜又滿足，接著卻打開了社群媒體。

Her classmates were sharing photos from a concert. One friend had visited a beautiful café, and another was traveling with her family. Mia looked at her own day again. Suddenly, reading at home did not seem exciting enough. She began to wonder whether she had missed something important.
同學們正在分享演唱會照片，有人去了漂亮的咖啡館，也有人和家人旅行。Mia 回頭看自己的這一天，突然覺得在家讀書似乎不夠精彩。她開始懷疑自己是否錯過了重要的事情。

This feeling is often called the fear of missing out, or FOMO. People may feel it when they see others having experiences they do not have. Social media makes these experiences easy to see, but a picture only shows a small part of someone’s life.
這種感覺常稱為錯失恐懼（FOMO）。當人們看到別人擁有自己沒有的經驗時，就可能產生這種感受。社群媒體讓這些經驗隨手可見，但照片往往只呈現生活的一小部分。

Mia decided to put her phone away and think about what she truly enjoyed. Her day had not become worse because someone else had gone to a concert. She still remembered laughing with her brother and finishing a wonderful chapter of her book.
Mia 決定放下手機，想想自己真正喜歡的事。別人去了演唱會，並不會讓她的一天變差。她依然記得和弟弟一起笑，以及讀完精彩書籍章節的快樂。

The next time Mia saw exciting photos online, she tried a simple question: “Do I want this experience, or do I only want to look as happy as the people in the picture?” The question did not remove every uncomfortable feeling, but it helped her choose how to spend her time.
下一次看到社群上的精彩照片時，Mia 試著問自己：「我是想要這種經驗，還是只想看起來和照片裡的人一樣快樂？」這個問題沒有消除所有不舒服的感受，卻幫助她更有意識地安排時間。

intermediate.title: The Quiet Saturday That Suddenly Felt Inadequate
paras: Until she opened social media, Mia had considered her Saturday a success. She had enjoyed a novel, prepared lunch with her father, and helped her brother solve a difficult math problem. Yet photographs of friends at concerts and fashionable cafés made her ordinary afternoon feel strangely disappointing. Nothing about her day had changed; what had changed was the standard by which she judged it.
在打開社群媒體前，Mia 一直覺得自己的星期六過得不錯。她讀了小說、和爸爸煮午餐，也幫弟弟解出一道數學難題。然而，朋友在演唱會及時髦咖啡館的照片，卻讓這個平凡下午突然顯得令人失望。她的一天沒有改變，改變的是她用來評價這一天的標準。

Psychologists use the term fear of missing out, or FOMO, to describe anxiety that others may be enjoying rewarding experiences without us. Although the feeling existed long before smartphones, digital platforms can make comparisons more frequent. We are repeatedly shown carefully selected moments while remaining largely unaware of the boredom, disagreements, and routine that surround them.
心理學家使用「錯失恐懼」（FOMO）來描述一種焦慮：擔心別人正在享受有價值的經驗，而自己卻沒有參與。這種感受早在智慧型手機問世前就已存在，但數位平台可能讓比較變得更加頻繁。我們不斷看見別人精心挑選的瞬間，卻幾乎看不見背後的無聊、爭執與日常。

The difficulty is not that people share happy memories. Rather, it is that viewers may treat those selected images as a complete account of everyone else’s life. As a result, an enjoyable evening at home can appear less valuable than an event we never wanted to attend in the first place. The comparison quietly changes our priorities.
問題不在於人們分享快樂回憶，而在於觀看者可能把經過挑選的照片當成別人生活的全貌。因此，即使原本很享受在家度過的夜晚，也可能覺得它不如自己原本根本不想參加的活動有價值。這樣的比較悄悄改變了我們的優先順序。

Mia began experimenting with a small habit: before opening an app, she asked what she expected to gain from it. Was she looking for a message from a friend, useful information, or simply relief from boredom? This pause helped her notice when she was scrolling automatically rather than intentionally.
Mia 開始嘗試一個小習慣：每次打開 App 前，先問自己希望從中獲得什麼。她是在等朋友訊息、尋找有用資訊，還是單純想擺脫無聊？這短暫的停頓讓她察覺自己何時是在無意識滑手機，而非有目的地使用。

Her experience suggests that a healthier relationship with social media does not necessarily require avoiding it altogether. Instead, it may begin with recognizing a simple distinction: observing someone else’s happiness is not evidence that our own life is lacking.
她的經驗顯示，與社群媒體建立更健康的關係，不一定得完全遠離它。相反地，起點可能是認清一個簡單的區別：看見別人的快樂，並不代表自己的生活有所欠缺。

advanced.title: When Curated Happiness Becomes a Measuring Stick
paras: Mia’s Saturday had been, by any reasonable standard, satisfying. She had read without interruption, cooked with her father, and helped her younger brother overcome a frustrating homework problem. Nevertheless, after encountering an endless succession of photographs documenting concerts, travel, and stylish restaurants, she found herself reconsidering what had seemed like a perfectly worthwhile day. The experience illustrates a curious feature of social comparison: satisfaction can deteriorate even when the underlying circumstances remain unchanged.
從任何合理標準來看，Mia 的星期六都很充實。她不受打擾地閱讀、和父親下廚，並協助弟弟克服令人挫折的作業難題。然而，在接連看見演唱會、旅行與時髦餐廳的照片後，她開始重新評價原本覺得很值得的一天。這段經驗說明社會比較的一個微妙特性：即使實際情況完全沒有改變，滿足感仍可能下降。

The fear of missing out, commonly abbreviated as FOMO, refers to unease arising from the possibility that others are enjoying experiences from which we are absent. Digital platforms do not create the desire to belong; that desire is deeply familiar to human beings. What these platforms can change, however, is the frequency and visibility of opportunities for comparison, allowing countless selectively presented lives to compete for our attention.
錯失恐懼（FOMO）指的是一種不安：擔心別人正在享受自己未能參與的經驗。數位平台並非創造了人們想要歸屬的渴望；這種渴望本來就是人類熟悉的感受。然而，平台可能改變比較機會出現的頻率與可見度，讓無數經過選擇呈現的生活片段爭奪我們的注意力。

The distinction between representation and reality is therefore crucial. A photograph records an occasion, not the emotional texture of an entire week. Yet when selected highlights are repeatedly mistaken for ordinary life, viewers may evaluate their unedited routines against an unrealistic reference point. In such circumstances, the apparent inadequacy of one’s own experience is partly a consequence of the comparison itself.
因此，區分呈現方式與現實至關重要。照片記錄的是某個場合，而不是整個星期的情緒樣貌。然而，當精選亮點一再被誤認為日常生活，觀看者便可能拿自己未經修飾的生活，與不切實際的參照標準比較。在這種情況下，自己的經驗看似不足，有一部分其實是比較行為本身造成的。

It would be misleading, however, to conclude that social media is inherently harmful. Online communities can provide friendship, inspiration, and practical information, particularly for people whose interests are not shared by those around them. The more meaningful question concerns the conditions under which connection turns into competition—and whether users can recognize that transition before it shapes their decisions.
然而，若因此認定社群媒體本質上有害，也會造成誤導。網路社群可以帶來友誼、靈感與實用資訊，對於周遭缺乏同好的人尤其如此。更有意義的問題在於：連結在什麼條件下變成競爭？使用者能否在它影響決定之前察覺這個轉變？

Mia eventually developed a modest rule: she would check social media with a purpose rather than use it whenever silence felt uncomfortable. This strategy did not make comparison disappear, nor could it guarantee lasting contentment. It did, however, return one important decision to her: the authority to determine whether her day had been meaningful.
後來 Mia 建立了一條簡單原則：使用社群媒體應帶著目的，而非每當安靜讓她不自在時就打開它。這項策略不會讓比較完全消失，也無法保證永久滿足；但它的確讓一項重要決定重新回到她手中：由自己判斷這一天是否有意義。

patterns.meaning: 這顯示／暗示……；用於審慎推論
patterns.example: This suggests that comparison can change how we evaluate our lives.
patterns.tip: 若證據不足以確定因果，suggests 通常比 proves 更恰當。

patterns.example: In terms of personal satisfaction, a quiet day can still be meaningful.
patterns.tip: 不可寫成 in terms to。

patterns.example: Although the photos seemed exciting, Mia valued her own experience.
patterns.tip: 英文正式寫作中，Although 子句後不再另外接 but。

patterns.frame: It is worth considering whether + 子句
patterns.example: It is worth considering whether online comparison affects our choices.
patterns.tip: 適合議論文提出問題或轉換論述角度。

beginner.q: What made Mia question her Saturday?
options: A phone call from her father
beginner.why: 第二段提到她看到同學的照片後開始覺得自己的週末不夠精彩。

intermediate.q: What does the writer suggest about social-media photos?
options: They are usually impossible to understand
They represent selected moments rather than whole lives
intermediate.why: 第三段指出觀看者可能把精選圖片誤當成完整人生。

intermediate.q: Why does Mia pause before opening an app?
options: To decide whether she has a purpose
To turn off all notifications forever
To compare her photos with others
To avoid speaking to her brother
intermediate.why: 第四段說明她先釐清打開 App 的目的。

advanced.q: Which assumption does the author most directly challenge?
options: An exciting photograph represents ordinary life
People sometimes compare themselves with others
advanced.why: 第三段指出照片並不能代表一整週的情緒樣貌，挑戰把精選亮點視為日常的假設。

advanced.q: What best describes the author’s attitude toward social media?
advanced.why: 第四段同時指出社群媒體的風險及潛在益處，觀點有所保留且平衡。

reflections: Is a meaningful day necessarily an exciting one? Explain your view.
How could a student use social media without relying on it to judge personal success?
